next.reason: §2023:8.3.5 SR9 repeats that a space may follow any separator 'except the opening delimiter of a literal' (1985: opening quotation mark) and that such a space is part of the literal; §2023:8.3.5 SR8 b) keeps the literal side. Picture and numeric-literal punctuation is still a symbol: comma, semicolon and period separate only before a space (§2023:8.3.5 SR2, SR3), parentheses except in a picture string (§2023:8.3.5 SR4). The literal-content exemption sits in the uncataloged 8.3.5 preamble ('except when appearing in a literal'); 2023 has no comment-entries, whose removal is recorded on the rules that carried them. Same programs accepted and refused.
